title: TwoSidedConvolutionalPerceptron.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Strict separation of N = samples + 1 signed feature vectors by the bilinear margin m_i(c,v) = c₁⟨D_i,v⟩ + c₂⟨shift D_i,v⟩. The constraints are nonconvex in the joint parameters (c,v); no optimization objective is specified.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query (i,θ) returns the exact gradient of the individual bilinear margin with respect to θ. Replies are independent of history and oracle seed; there is no oracle error.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same component query also returns the exact scalar margin m_i(θ), with value and gradient counted as one oracle call.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Features lie in Euclidean ℝ^d, d > 0; parameters lie in ℝ² × ℝ^d. The shift is a cyclic coordinate permutation.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Write g = lower, R = upper, μ = contrast, κ = margin. Hidden data satisfy D_i = b_i a + μu_i, a = ones/√d, g ≤ |b_i| ≤ R, ⟨a,u_i⟩ = 0, and ‖u_i‖ ≤ 1/√2. A hidden unit vector s satisfies ⟨(u_i − shift u_i)/√2,s⟩ ≥ κ for every i. Background signs may differ. All six Params fields are public. Validity requires 0 < g ≤ R, μ > 0, κ > 0 and κμB ≤ 3R/2, where B = ⌈2²⁴(R/g)²(1 + log(1 + g/μ))/κ³⌉. Allowed algorithms start at ((1,0),0), query components cyclically, and use a fixed positive step size, updating only when the queried margin is nonpositive.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/TwoSidedConvolutionalPerceptron.lean: Geometry, derivative, Params, family, spec.publicInput, spec.valid; LongTails/Setups/ManySampleConvolutionalPerceptron.lean: axis.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The final output must satisfy m_i(θ) > 0 for every sample. There is no epsilon tolerance, normalized output-margin requirement, or objective-gap criterion.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: Success is required for every seed outcome, not merely almost surely or in expectation. The supplied budget is the fixed total N B component-oracle calls, including queries that cause no update.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/TwoSidedConvolutionalPerceptron.lean: spec.successful, family; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace, Convergence; supplied extracted result budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: This separation problem combines signed constant backgrounds, centered defects with a common discrete-derivative separator, a contrast-dependent validity regime, and a prescribed cyclic bilinear update family.

descriptionHtml:
Two-Sided Convolutional Perceptron

We study strict separation of vectors b0,…,bn∈Rd by a convolutional perceptron with parameters θ=((a,c),w)∈R2×Rd and margin mi(θ)=a⟨bi,w⟩+c⟨Sbi,w⟩, where S is the cyclic shift by one coordinate. Each vector has a constant background of either sign, bounded above and away from zero in magnitude, plus a bounded centered defect. The scaled differences between defects and their shifts share a unit separator with positive margin. The oracle returns the margin and its parameter derivative for a queried sample. Starting from ((1,0),0), cyclic perceptron updates must produce an output θ¯ with mi(θ¯)>0 for every sample and every realization.

Write d≥1 and n≥0 for integers, so there are n+1 samples. Inner products and norms on Rd are Euclidean. With coordinates indexed by j=0,…,d−1, define (Su)j=u(j−1)modd,e=1d(1,…,1),Tu=u−Su2. The task is to find parameters whose margins are strictly positive simultaneously. The algorithm receives d,n,g,R,μ,κ; the data vectors and their geometric decomposition are accessed only through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Parameter regime). The background bounds g,R, contrast μ, and derivative margin κ satisfy 0<g≤R,μ>0,κ>0. They also obey κμ⌈224(Rg)21+log⁡(1+g/μ)κ3⌉≤3R2, where log is the natural logarithm and the ceiling denotes the least integer greater than or equal to its positive argument.

Assumption 2 (Two-sided background and defect separation). There exist scalars βi∈R, defects ui∈Rd, and a vector v∈Rd such that ∥v∥=1 and, for every i=0,…,n, bi=βie+μui,g≤|βi|≤R,⟨e,ui⟩=0,∥ui∥≤12,⟨Tui,v⟩≥κ.

For a query (i,θ)∈{0,…,n}×(R2×Rd), the oracle returns the exact pair (mi(θ),hi(θ)), where mi(((a,c),w))=a⟨bi,w⟩+c⟨Sbi,w⟩,hi(((a,c),w))=((⟨bi,w⟩,⟨Sbi,w⟩),abi+cSbi).

Our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze the two-sided convolutional perceptron with cyclic sample queries and a fixed step size η>0. The algorithm chooses η from its available inputs and initializes θ0=((1,0),0),i0=0. At each call t, it queries (it,θt) and applies θt+1={θt+ηhit(θt),mit(θt)≤0,θt,mit(θt)>0,it+1=(it+1)mod(n+1). Thus the sample index advances even when the parameters remain unchanged. After an allotted number K≥0 of oracle calls, the output is the last iterate θ¯=θK. The required accuracy is strict separation: mi(θ¯)>0for every i=0,…,n, for every realization of any algorithm randomness.

source:
import LongTails.Setups.ManySampleConvolutionalPerceptron

open OracleTemplate
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.TwoSidedConvolutionalPerceptron

abbrev Features := TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.Features
abbrev Space := ManySampleConvolutionalPerceptron.Space
abbrev Reply := ManySampleConvolutionalPerceptron.Reply
noncomputable abbrev axis := ManySampleConvolutionalPerceptron.axis
abbrev Data (d n : ℕ) := Fin (n + 1) → Features d
abbrev Query (d n : ℕ) := Fin (n + 1) × Space d

noncomputable def derivative {d : ℕ} (u : Features d) : Features d :=
  (Real.sqrt 2)⁻¹ • (u - TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.shift u)

structure Geometry {d n : ℕ} (D : Data d n) (g R μ κ : ℝ) where
  background : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ
  defect : Fin (n + 1) → Features d
  separator : Features d
  sample_eq : ∀ i, D i = background i • axis d + μ • defect i
  background_lower : ∀ i, g ≤ |background i|
  background_upper : ∀ i, |background i| ≤ R
  centered : ∀ i, ⟪axis d, defect i⟫ = 0
  defect_norm : ∀ i, ‖defect i‖ ≤ (Real.sqrt 2)⁻¹
  separator_unit : ‖separator‖ = 1
  derivative_margin : ∀ i, κ ≤ ⟪derivative (defect i), separator⟫

noncomputable def answer {d n : ℕ} (D : Data d n) (query : Query d n) : Reply d :=
  ⟨TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.margin .conv d (D query.1) query.2,
    TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.direction .conv d (D query.1) query.2⟩

def Separates {d n : ℕ} (D : Data d n) (θ : Space d) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, 0 < TwoSampleQuadraticPerceptron.margin .conv d (D i) θ

noncomputable def identityStart (d : ℕ) : Space d := ((1, 0), 0)

structure Params where
  dimension : ℕ
  samples : ℕ
  lower : ℝ
  upper : ℝ
  contrast : ℝ
  margin : ℝ

def family (p : Params)
    (A : Algorithm (Query p.dimension p.samples) (Reply p.dimension) (Space p.dimension)) :
    Prop :=
  ∃ (point : A.State → Space p.dimension) (index : A.State → Fin (p.samples + 1)) (η : ℝ),
    0 < η ∧
    (∀ seed, point (A.initial seed) = identityStart p.dimension ∧ index (A.initial seed) = 0) ∧
    (∀ s, A.query s = (0, (index s, point s))) ∧
    (∀ s r, point (A.update s r) =
      if r.margin ≤ 0 then point s + η • r.direction else point s) ∧
    (∀ s r, index (A.update s r) = finRotate (p.samples + 1) (index s)) ∧
    (∀ s, A.output s = point s)

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Data p.dimension p.samples
  Query p := Query p.dimension p.samples
  Reply p := Reply p.dimension
  Output p := Space p.dimension
  publicInput := id
  valid p :=
    0 < p.dimension ∧ 0 < p.lower ∧ p.lower ≤ p.upper ∧ 0 < p.contrast ∧ 0 < p.margin ∧
      p.margin * p.contrast * ⌈2 ^ 24 * (p.upper / p.lower) ^ 2 *
        (1 + Real.log (1 + p.lower / p.contrast)) / p.margin ^ 3⌉₊ ≤ 3 * p.upper / 2
  admissible p D oracle :=
    Nonempty (Geometry D p.lower p.upper p.contrast p.margin) ∧
    ∀ history query seed, oracle.answer history query seed = answer D query.2
  successful _ D output _ := ∀ ω, Separates D (output ω)
  allowedAlgorithm := family

end LongTails.Setups.TwoSidedConvolutionalPerceptron
